_comment: S3 bucket policy — agrisync-raw-ap-south-1. PHASE 1 (safe to apply now).
spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN §11 (S11-infra-author)
LIVE STATE CAPTURED 2026-08-15 (read-only, aws s3api get-bucket-policy):
NoSuchBucketPolicy — this bucket has NO policy today. Rollback:
aws s3api delete-bucket-policy --bucket agrisync-raw-ap-south-1 --region ap-south-1
This is PHASE 1 only — TLS-only + 'some encryption header present' deny
rails. It deliberately does NOT require a specific algorithm or a specific
KMS key. Live encryption on this bucket today (captured 2026-08-15, read-
only aws s3api get-bucket-encryption) is SSE-S3 AES256 with
BucketKeyEnabled=true — NOT the customer-managed KMS key the plan intends
('under AES256, not the intended customer-managed key' — gap register I4).
This policy is written to be satisfied by that CURRENT state, so applying
it today changes nothing about what encryption objects get; it only
closes the 'no policy at all' gap and blocks unencrypted / non-TLS access.
PHASE 2 (a SEPARATE, NOT-YET-SAFE file: bucket-policy-cmk-deny-rail.
PHASE2-DO-NOT-APPLY.json) tightens this to require the dedicated CMK
specifically. Do not fold that statement into this file and do not apply
it until the ordering trap in that file's header is resolved by the
backend team (unswallow the failure -> bind RawBlobStore config with
ValidateOnStart -> only then add the CMK deny rail). Applying the CMK
requirement before the key is bound makes every PUT fail with the
exception silently swallowed by the current write path — farmers would
get HTTP 200s while their evidence silently stopped being retained. That
code change is out of this lane's scope (src/, not aws/).
APPLY (founder only): aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket agrisync-raw-ap-south-1 --policy file://bucket-policy.json --region ap-south-1
(apply-config.sh does this as part of the single transaction.)
VERIFY: aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket agrisync-raw-ap-south-1 --region ap-south-1 | jq -r '.Policy | fromjson | .Statement[].Sid'
